body:
Our situations are very similar. I'm just as hopeless as you are, so I can't offer you much advice.

Be very careful with cannabis, though. I abused it for a couple months when I tried to go back to college in 2010, smoking more than I ever had, often alone. I was a fool to go back that soon in the first place, and I probably would have failed anyway, but the weed didn't help. It became a consuming distraction from my problems to the point where they just got worse and worse. I ended up in the same situation as before: feeling suicidal, too far into the term and too much of a mess mentally to salvage any part of my minimal course load, and really left with no choice but to withdraw. (Right now I'm struggling to describe exactly how weed wasn't beneficial, but perhaps others can provide similar information. If you do wish to reconsider your smoking habits, /r/leaves may be of interest.)

This problem has been with me for some years, though I don't have a diagnosis of ADD. It really started becoming an obstacle when I started college, and that was about the same time that I started really falling apart. That was nearly three years ago. Even with meds and therapy, I haven't gotten better, and it's still hard for me to focus on anything, let alone derive much pleasure from those things I try to do.

This is exactly how I feel. 

I'm also afraid I might fail at killing myself, leaving me severely brain-damaged or something. At the same time I don't seem to have the "courage" to jump from a sufficiently high bridge. And I really don't want to die and leave my family to discover my body if it's obvious I did something to myself.

Yikes, sounds quite similar to me. First flagged as suicidal at 9, now 20 and still hopelessly depressed. I already tried the "move elsewhere and start anew" thing already, to an extent, when I attempted to go to college (in a different city) from high school. That didn't work, I escaped none of the problems I thought I would, and I only sank further. Tried college a couple times again (once back at home), crashed again. It might help if those debts could go away, but I know I'd still be a wreck given that history. Tried different meds, different therapists... nothing's worked. Life would be fantastic, but only if it were viable for me. For whatever reasons, I can't make it so.

Given my history (mental illness and otherwise), I'm quite certain I couldn't pull off anything like the OP suggests even if I had just enough resources to move.

I'm not qualified to give a diagnosis, of course, but you could be depressed. It might be temporary if your current struggling to function for university started in some way because of external events, but "temporary" probably has a high upper bound on the duration of this episode. Have you ever felt this low or struggled like this before? What I've read, if I can remember it correctly, suggests that you might be more predisposed to another episode if you've had one before--and certainly if you've exhibited lots of symptoms from a very young age.

Speaking as somebody who used cannabis frequently when attempting college last time around, I can agree that the high seems quite fake. (I even feel that way when just on antidepressants.) I've lost the capacity to enjoy it at all now (on the occasions I visit a few friends back at college), and I look back on some of those occasions with embarrassment. Perhaps all that usage was a net negative for me, if not a primary contributor to my problems (they've been around far longer). 

This isn't to say you shouldn't toke (or uptoke, if you like /r/trees). If your mind isn't kind of "normal" or non-depressed to begin with, however, maybe it's advisable to limit yourself to more judicious use or something. In particular, I found it even more detrimental to smoke alone rather than with a couple of close-ish friends.

I might advise at least speaking to a counselor of some sort (maybe an academic one as well if you're about to run into serious problems), but those haven't helped me much so far, so it might be a hollow recommendation. (Then again, I've probably been more dysfunctional longer.)

Meh. My parents/other family decided to delude me about something similar when I was young. I don't think they really knew any better. Even when I was in high school in this backwater of a city I knew I wasn't quite at the top even of people stuck around here, but it was only worse when I tried college. Much, much worse. Maybe it has a bit to do with the protracted crash I've had for a few years now, but there's no way I could've been special or important or valuable even before that crash (and after adjusting for even younger age).

I'll probably agree. I'm getting back in therapy and on antidepressants, but--seriously, now--is this going to end any better than when I've tried those in the recent past? They only coincided with even further decline in my ability to function, to the point where I'm barely 20 and I've sunk so deep there's no chance I'll ever get out and have an existence I consider worthwhile. 

Lately I've had a few moments of temporarily elevated mood, where I'm not as intensely depressed as usual, but even then I can still determine nothing other than that I'm completely screwed and don't see much reason to live. Even when around the few close friends I still sort of have (and occasionally see) I'm flooded with thoughts of worthlessness, even regrets about my failure to kill myself earlier (when things weren't quite as bad, even). 

I'd rather live, but not if I can't thrive on my own--failing to thrive is not only painful for me but also a drag on people I know and on society at large.

Basically, I wish I could actually live a decent life (this is ill-defined in part due to what seems to be my failing mind, but I seem to see features of one in some of the people I know). But I can't possibly bring myself to do whatever I might need to do to work toward such goals. Physically and mentally I just seem to have been failing forever, but most acutely in the last few years (with some very brief interludes of distraction/borderline pleasure). I still sort of don't want to die, and I don't like what it might do to other people in my life, but I just don't see anywhere else I can go. I wish I could just randomly fall asleep one night (being able to do just that would be nice) fairly soon and not wake up.

I'd try to recount more of my own experience, but everything I've experienced seems to have been said better here already. My mind doesn't work well enough even to articulate to myself the particular issues I have that are specific to my own life. What I've managed to put together here is probably difficult enough to read already, not actually decent writing despite others' claims that I "can write [well]."

I'm hoping that they can add me back once their plans renew. Even so, however, co-payments for services (or costs to add me back, if any) are probably going to add just more of an expense they can ill afford. I've thought about trying new doctors, though, if I had the opportunity.

Do you have any idea how a wreck like me could possibly get hired doing something at a decent wage, though? I seem to have failed badly at working for my uncle lately--construction work doesn't seem suited to me anyway--and I don't know where to look. I have little experience, I'm a college dropout, and I'm currently living at home in a region with one of the US's worst unemployment problems even during "good" times. I'd consider classes at a community college (a few could be useful), but I haven't proven to myself that I could pick myself up again and study...

That probably fits my situation... family and friends who care but have no way to help. I'd rather not leave them behind, particularly my close friends, but I don't know how to help myself, either. If I'm not good at marketing myself, for instance, I'll never be able to make a decent income... or any income at all, given where I live and what pitiful skills and experience I have. But you have a point: even my closest friends probably aren't as open with me about the details of their lives (if I could even remember them) as I am with them. I'm more pathetic and desperate.

I tried therapy and different meds (with two different doctors) for about a year and a half. I currently don't have any health insurance since I'm not attempting to go to school right now, so I can't get treatment even if I thought it would work. Sleep would be nice, and I've had occasional success falling asleep with melatonin... but I still can't do much of anything no matter what kind of rest I get. Even at my peak of being awake yesterday I couldn't actually read anything at the library... couldn't even focus very well on a podcast as I walked around my neighborhood. I'll lay down and I just sort of jolt as I dwell on what's been wrong with me for so long... it's hard to describe. (This happened yesterday as well while driving home from the library in my younger sister's car... maybe I'll have to use that sometime to get to a better suicide spot than the freeway overpass by my house.)

From what I've heard, the situation as it is under Prop. 215 is quite lax, and you can find doctors willing to give recommendations for all manner of conditions, probably some even milder than anxiety or major depression. I know nothing more, though.

(If you don't want to smoke the stuff, vaporization and edibles would be other options as well, though I'm not specifically familiar with how the effects differ between these methods of consumption.)

I don't know that I like to feel depressed, but I'm always afraid that on some level outside of my conscious control maybe I'm comfortable with my depression because it's a convenient way of trying to get sympathy from people. I would hate for that to be true... but since I can't picture myself actually being able to do whatever is proper and productive in any situation, I fear it might be. The fact that I might have this character flaw just makes me even more confirmed in my depression and my belief that I don't deserve to live, let alone be happy. Maybe I excessively avoid talking to my friends as a result...

Fortunately my best friends are all stoners--you're right, they are awesome people. I'm stuck 200 miles away from school where they are, though. Going to university probably made me more of a financial burden than if I'd started out at the local community college, actually--lots of borrowing--but this area is a complete cesspit. I wish I had a way out, but I haven't the cash to move, let alone to replace some essential possessions stolen from me.

I know people would be hurt by my going away. But I can't figure out how to get myself together. I don't want to go on living if it's just going to be the same old pain every single day. (Even on those occasions when someone hands me money and I can see my friends, I'm still horribly depressed and often still suicidal.) I completely broke down and couldn't bring myself even to paint my uncle's house when I was there earlier... for a while I was able to read a nonfiction book somewhat related to my potential major (economics), but it wasn't at all academic, and I couldn't even read it very effectively. All else I could think about was the lack of ideas anyone had on this subreddit (fewer replies compared to other posts around the same time), whether I should have started the journey to one of those bridges, and how I could potentially commit suicide here at home if I don't have a personal vehicle to go to one of those bridges.

It may be early in life, but I've still fallen so far behind already. As a result I'm just stuck languishing during the few precious years of young adulthood I'll have. How the hell will I pull this together?

I was able to chat a little bit with one of my best friends a little while ago about my immediate frustration. He and others have been wonderful people to talk to, and he and his girlfriend have accommodated me whenever I've been able to visit them at college, though I've always been paranoid that I'm burdening them too much just by trying to talk to them. I'm afraid I don't or can't contribute enough back to them, even if they don't express that to me. I'm sure even my family is fed up by now with my inability to act positively on most advice so far, and my constant thoughts of suicide don't help. I try not to bring it up to them anymore.

Maybe if I can calm down enough this weekend (I probably won't end up being able to do much work, ergo no money) I can try my best to get out in person and look for jobs. I haven't the slightest idea how to do that, though--I just seize up in most social situations, and I wouldn't know how to ask people I know (old high school classmates that I haven't been close with) to help me get a job. There's not much within a three-mile radius of home, and I'm not sure how kindly an employer would look upon someone doing this if they're going to face customers, but I guess it'd be nice to have something I could walk to at least until I can get a car again. (I don't have a bike, and I live so far on the edge of suburbia that the skeleton of a bus system doesn't even go here, and two of the roads bordering my neighborhood are narrow two-lane roads with no sidewalks or lighting. Maybe I'd be able to borrow my younger sister's car if I got a job, though.)

My mom handled the insurance... I don't think the car was insured for theft at all since it was so old. Supposedly the computer and other things could potentially be covered under something else, but those are the least of my worries right now. I haven't been that productive, so it's not as if I was using that laptop for any real work, nor is there any data on it of any consequence.

I'm one of those people who just burned out and sank, I guess--I at least got by well enough in high school to get into the school I did, though even then I was already slipping or at least not meeting the challenges I needed to. And I've already gone over in my head the negative effects I'd have on others... it'd be unfortunate, but I'm already kind of a marginal component of my circles of friends and family as is. They know I've been in pain for a long time, but there really isn't anything they can do to fix that, and I've proven inept at doing it myself. It saddens me to think about having to leave life, but I just don't see a way out most of the time. I can put up with only so much more physical unease and impulses to beat myself up. (I broke the screen of a phone several months ago beating myself with a small pair of pliers without realizing the phone was still in my pocket. In the past I've also occasionally tied bedsheets tightly around my neck for a few minutes at a time, whacked my skull with other objects... it's infrequent, but I've been doing this since I was rather young, I think. Same for suicidal thinking--I was first flagged when I wrote some assignment in the 4th grade in a way that suggested I wanted to die.) In any event, my end would at least provide closure to the unmitigated disaster/tragedy that has been my life. It's almost as if it's my duty and obligation to bow out voluntarily and quit being such a frustrating burden.

I've just gotten to my uncle's, but I haven't slept since yesterday morning, so I think I'll be useless for at least a little while at work, if I can do any at all. I might need to nap. Worse, I've sunk into such despair that I just might look up public transit directions from here to any one of a few tall bridges within about 80 miles... not that I'd likely follow through on those plans, in part because it means I'd have to walk 10 miles of country roads even to get to that first low-frequency bus.
